reason: Conversation 1 asked more useful questions (filter and blockage, a full direct charge, the swelling/heat check). It answered the homeowner's actual question, that a new battery is the likely fix, and told them to ask Dyson for a genuine pack quote and match the SV12 model. Its weaknesses are wrongly assuming the guarantee might still apply, an invented '95%' figure, and encouraging third-party packs with only a loose quality caveat. Conversation 2 used the wrong light cues (orange/green), asked the customer to remove the battery after they had said they would not, and wrongly said an 'engineer is needed' when the pack is user-fittable. It did usefully push towards Dyson support and a quote, but it never explicitly confirmed a V10 battery as the likely fix or gave any part guidance.
